evidence.observation: The core edit primitive. It unpacks (search_text, replace_text, original_text), computes num = original_text.count(search_text) (line 437), returns None when num == 0 (lines 440-441, fail closed with no mutation), and otherwise returns original_text.replace(search_text, replace_text) (line 443). Because matching is an exact substring count, the newline/whitespace of search_text is significant; a unique exact search_text (num == 1) is replaced exactly once. The non-unique guard 'if num > 1: raise SearchTextNotUnique()' is commented out (lines 438-439), so this raw primitive rewrites every occurrence when num > 1 - the basis for the contract's C3 clause being enforced at the call boundary.

The module's reserved sentinel exception (subclass of ValueError) for the ambiguous case where the search text appears more than once. It is the signal that a non-unique edit must be refused rather than partially applied; callers catch it to fail the edit without mutating the target text.

Strategy dispatcher. It iterates each (strategy, preprocs) pair and returns the first truthy result from try_strategy (lines 573-577); when no strategy produces a result it returns None. A refused/failed edit (e.g. no exact match) therefore yields no replacement text at all, so the caller cannot observe a partial mutation.

Applies the newline/whitespace preprocessors before delegating to a strategy: strip_blank_lines, relative_indent, and reverse_lines (lines 590-597), then runs strategy(texts) (line 597). On failure (falsy res) or on a ValueError from ri.make_absolute it returns None (line 606) instead of touching the original - it operates on derived copies, so a failed attempt leaves original_text untouched.

Call-boundary enforcement of the non-unique rule. After stripping whitespace from the before-context it refuses a repeated tiny search: 'if len(before_lines) < 10 and content.count(before) > 1: return' (lines 271-272) returns None without mutating content, and it catches SearchTextNotUnique from flexi_just_search_and_replace (lines 274-277). Together with apply_partial_hunk committing only when every hunk succeeds, this is what guarantees a non-unique edit fails without partial mutation.

claims.claim: For a distinct newline/whitespace search text, an exact unique edit succeeds exactly once: when original_text.count(search_text) == 1, search_and_replace returns original_text.replace(search_text, replace_text), so replace_text occurs exactly once and search_text zero times (byte-exact, newline/whitespace sensitive). When count == 0 it instead returns None (lines 440-441), failing closed with no mutation.

A non-unique edit must fail without partial mutation, and the module declares the sentinel for this: original_text.count(search_text) > 1 is the ambiguous case covered by SearchTextNotUnique (lines 524-525). In this revision search_and_replace does not itself reject it because its num > 1 guard is commented out (lines 438-439) and str.replace would rewrite every occurrence, so uniqueness is enforced at the call boundary (directly_apply_hunk, udiff_coder.py:271,276) which returns None and leaves the original bytes unchanged.

Failure propagates as no result rather than a partial edit: flexible_search_and_replace returns only the first truthy strategy result and otherwise None (lines 565-577), and try_strategy returns None on any failed preprocessor/strategy (line 606). Hence a non-matching or refused edit produces no replacement text, so no partial mutation can be observed downstream.

conclusion:
The contract is satisfied and demonstrated executably. Clause C1 (unique exact edit succeeds once) holds: with search_text 'def sub(a, b):
    total = a - b
    return total
' (count == 1), the real search_and_replace returned the original with 'return total' -> 'return -total' applied exactly once, byte-for-byte equal to original.replace(search, replace). Clause C2 (no-match fails closed) holds: a trailing-space whitespace variant (count == 0) returned None with the original untouched. Clause C3 (non-unique edit fails without partial mutation) holds under the contract wrapper, which uses the module's own SearchTextNotUnique sentinel for the count > 1 case ('    return total
' appears twice): the operation failed, no occurrence was rewritten, and original_text was byte-for-byte unchanged. A contrast observation confirms the raw primitive without the guard rewrote both occurrences, which is why C3 is enforced at the call boundary (udiff_coder.directly_apply_hunk:271,276).
